cells.tense: You are here, and the pull you steer by is one you have already recognised as yours.
cells.ask: Tell one person the shape of something you've noticed — not the conclusion, just the pattern — and let it stand without defending it.
cells.core: You can feel which direction is yours, and you're not arguing with it. The pull toward what you actually want has steadiness to it, and it comes from something that finished growing rather than something you're still forcing. What you cultivated has ripened enough to show, and it shows.\n\nSeeing how a thing works beneath its surface isn't only for you. That clarity moves outward — people catch it in how you put things, what you notice first, what you leave alone. Nothing in you is straining to prove the light is real. You're standing in the pattern and the pattern is standing in you, and the two of you are easy together. That ease is the thing, and it isn't accidental.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is yours and you're already showing it.
cells.verb: following a pull you recognise rather than one you were handed
cells.place: where a pattern is seen without its content, in the mind's ripening

cells.tense: You will have already reached a future you keep trying to write into being ahead of time.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about what's in front of you right now, out loud, and stop before you add what it could become.
cells.core: You're shining at a version of this that hasn't arrived, trying to make it arrive by brightness. The push has glow to it, but it dazzles more than it shows. People near you get light in their eyes instead of a way to see. You're standing ahead of the moment, and the moment can't catch up.\n\nReading how a thing works doesn't need a demonstration. The proof you keep offering sits between you and the contact it was meant to make, and the target slides past today. Stand in one unlit moment as it is and let that be enough. The pattern doesn't need you to arrive early. It needs you to stop moving the target out past what's here.
cells.sheetLine: You keep lighting a future that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.verb: following a pull you recognise rather than one you were handed

cells.tense: You were hoping for something that didn't come, and you are still standing at that door.
cells.ask: Pick one small thing that is actually growing right now and give it ten minutes of care — water, note, follow-up — nothing more.
cells.core: What was being tended didn't open the way it was supposed to, and the pull that used to orient you has gone quiet — not gone, quiet. You're where you were when it stopped, and staying there has become its own kind of tired.\n\nSeeing how things work under their surfaces has thinned out. Nothing's been fed. Following a pull needs somewhere for it to land, and you've stopped giving it anything to land on. One small growing thing, cared for today, gives the pull a place to point again. That is not a cure. It is a place to stand while the pull finds its footing, and it asks nothing of you but ten minutes.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped tending, and the pull went quiet.
cells.verb: following a pull you recognise rather than one you were handed

cells.tense: You are already giving off something you haven't claimed as yours to give off.
cells.ask: Take one thing you've described as 'just noticing' or 'happening to see' and say instead that you saw it — the pattern, the shape, the way it fits.
cells.core: People pick something up from you — a steadiness, a clarity — and you speak as though the room were simply bright. The way you cut to how a thing works is doing real work on the people around you, and you file it under luck or under just being practical.\n\nThe light comes from development you did, and it's still coming, even unnamed. Holding what you've built without gripping it — that's the strength underneath this, and it's already operating. Naming what you noticed changes what the people near you can receive from you. Say it was yours, once, plainly, and watch what it does.
cells.sheetLine: You're already giving it off. Name it as yours.
